children: Tradeweb
, SEI Investments
, and StepStone
were among Wells Fargo's top picks with its initiation of 24 alternative asset managers, exchanges, and brokerages.
Analyst Daniel Welden said Ares Management
is the bank's favorite large-cap pick in the alts space, with StepStone

as its "higher-beta idea." Discussing the sector, "We favor credit and infrastructure medium term, but view the group as coiled into earnings season, with estimate resets potentially clearing the way for a rally on better-than-feared commentary," he wrote in a note to clients.
Other alternative asset managers rated Overweight in Wells Fargo's coverage are BlackRock
, Hamilton Lane
, and Brookfield Asset Management
In the brokers sector, Interactive Brokers
is the bank's top large-cap pick, with SEI
considered an "idiosyncratic self-help story mid-stream in a re-rating." The other Overweight names in the category are LPL Financial
and Wealthfront
For the exchange names, Tradeweb
is the secular call, as it gains market share in the expanding global debt market, and CME Group
is the defensive play with the most durable exposure to rate volatility. Those are the only two stocks rated Outperform in Wells Fargo's coverage.
Of the 24 stocks now covered by the bank, the only two rated Underweight are Intercontinental Exchange
and Pershing Square

title: TW, SEIC, STEP favored by Wells Fargo in new coverage of brokers, asset managers, and exchanges
